title: Audit export templates, signed manifests, and scheduled delivery SLA
creator: Aisha Malik
summary: Design and deliver a first-class scheduled export capability that produces cryptographically signed PDF/CSV audit packages with geo-filtered content and manifest checksums. Provide export templates for legal/compliance teams, SLA-driven delivery windows, and a console experience for monitoring and re-running shipments.
background: Customers in regulated industries need regular, verifiable audit packages that satisfy regional data residency and retention policies. Current ad-hoc exports are manual, lack tamper-evidence, and do not include deterministic manifests for delta-reconciliation. This work builds an export orchestration layer: template-driven package generation, signed manifests (SHA256 + signing key), residency-aware content selection, and a scheduler with retry/SLA tracking.
requirements:
1) Export formats: PDF (signed cover + index), CSV (normalized rows) and gzipped bundles.
2) Template system: legal and operational templates selectable per-tenant; include localized headers, retention metadata, and redaction flags.
3) Residency filter: tenant-scoped partitioning so exports only include data from allowed regions.
4) Signed manifest: file-level checksum list (SHA256) and a manifest.json signed with our export key; support customer-provided signing keys for Private deployments.
5) Scheduler: cron-like UI for recurring deliveries with timezone support, SLA window, and retry policy.
6) Delivery channels: S3 presigned URL, SFTP, and secure webhook with HMAC verification.
7) Console: status, last-run logs, size estimate, and per-tenant audit trail.
8) Rollback and re-run support for partial failures and delta exports to avoid full re-shipments.
9) Operational metrics: export success rate, time-to-prepare, average size, and cost estimate per export.
10) Security: KMS integration for manifest signing keys and audit logging of key usage.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A tenant can create and save an export template that includes format, residency filters, and delivery target.
2) Scheduler runs for at least one tenant, produces a signed bundle (PDF+CSV+manifest), and delivers via S3 presigned URL.
3) Manifest verifies: checksums match files and signature verifies with the configured key.
4) Console shows per-run status, size, and a link to delivery logs.
5) Exports respect retention filters: no data older than retention window or outside region is included.
6) Operational alerts firing if export fails 3 times in a row or SLA is missed.
7) Customer security review sign-off for manifest format and key handling documented.
success_metrics:
- Reduce manual export requests by 90% for customers on Compliance Ledger pilot.
- 99% of scheduled exports complete within SLA window (configurable, default 24 hours).
- Mean time to re-run a failed export < 30 minutes for support engineers.
- Adoption: 5 pilot customers enabled and 2 production tenants automated within two sprints.

risks_mitigations:
Risk: Export bundles may include accidentally redacted or missing records due to residency filter bugs. Mitigation: Add pre-flight dry-run mode that produces a manifest preview with counts per region and retention buckets.
Risk: Signing key compromise. Mitigation: Use KMS/HSM-backed keys, rotate keys per release, and support tenant-managed keys for Private deployments.
Risk: Large exports causing runtime spikes. Mitigation: Streaming generation with chunked writes to temporary object store and throttled concurrency per-tenant.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): Implement core template engine, signed manifest, S3 delivery, and console status. Enable 2 pilot tenants. Phase 1: Add CSV normalization, PDF cover pages, SFTP/webhook delivery, retry policies, and public docs. Phase 2: Tenant-managed keys, re-run UI, delta exports, and SLA dashboards. Default rollout to hosted tenants after security review and cost tuning.

open_questions:
1) Should manifests be versioned per export schema to support future changes? (suggest: yes, include schema_version field).
2) For Private deployments, do we require customer-provided signing keys or support tenant KMS integration first? (security leaning: support both, MVP enables customer-provided keys later).
3) Which retention edge-cases should be redacted vs omitted? Need legal guidance on PII vs aggregated records.
4) Cost allocation model: how should export egress/storage be charged for hosted tenants?
notes_for_engineering:
- ENG-49321 (streaming export API) must be completed before pilot.
- Use parquet->CSV normalization for consistent column ordering.
- Implement manifest signing using AWS KMS Sign API for hosted, with fallback HMAC for webhooks.
- Provide a dry-run mode that returns manifest and counts without emitting delivery.
- Ensure export generation is idempotent by using run_id and deterministic file naming.
- Add circuit-breaker to prevent simultaneous large exports for the same tenant.
customer_notes: Pilot customers will receive a signed PDF index and CSV exports linked via presigned S3 URL. Customer feedback session scheduled after first two runs to validate content, redaction, and delivery timing. Support will provide run-level logs on request.
